title: Connection gating strategies for dependency degradation
creator: Marco Chen
description: Design and implement a connection-gating layer and tenant-aware shedding policy to protect Redwood runtime from cascading failures in downstream stores (Redis, Kafka, Postgres). This ticket covers heuristics for admission control, probabilistic thinning, early-bail fast paths, circuit breaker integration, and multi-region failover coordination. Goal: keep API-level SLOs stable during partial dependency degradation and enable predictable, explainable degraded behavior rather than surprising outages.
acceptance_criteria: Gate exists as a per-service middleware that can be toggled by route and tenant
SLO-driven thresholds applied: when backend latency or connection saturation exceeds threshold, admissions reduce according to policy
Probabilistic thinning reduces request rate to unhealthy dependency by at least 30% under simulated store saturation, preserving overall gateway p95 latency
Circuit breaker events trigger documented fallback mode (stale-cache reads, degraded scoring, synthetic responses) with audit logs
Automated tests / chaos monkey scenario demonstrating graceful degradation across Redis/Kafka/Postgres in CI
Dashboard panels surfaced in Console for gate metrics (admitted, rejected, thinned, reasons) and per-tenant impact
tasks: Draft design doc describing policy primitives: thresholds, per-tenant budgets, weights, probabilistic function
Implement middleware skeleton and per-route config in runtime
Integrate with existing connection pool metrics and expose usage gauges
Add circuit breaker hooks to mark dependency health and to coordinate with gate
Implement two default policies: conservative (for enterprise) and aggressive (for bursty PLG)
Add e2e simulation harness to replay production traces with injected downstream slowdowns
Create console dashboards and alerting rules for gate-related signals
Run canary rollout and compare SLOs vs baseline under controlled load
comments: 2026-02-25 Marco Chen: Initial triage. Multiple incidents this quarter traced to saturated Redis pools and downstream DB spikes. We need a predictable degradation mechanism that operates before connection exhaustion and avoids global failures.

2026-02-27 Aisha Patel: Proposed primitives: admission token bucket per-tenant, global soft-cap, and a probabilistic drop function that depends on queue length and backend latency. Prefer avoiding sudden all-or-nothing shedding.

2026-03-01 SRE Review (Lena Romero): Request metrics to drive policy: backend p95 latency, active connections %, queue depth, and error rate. Recommend starting with threshold at 75% pool usage and p95 > 200ms for Redis as a trigger.

2026-03-03 Design feedback (Product, Oliver Grant): Need clear customer-visible degradation modes and an SLA-compatible messaging plan. For Dedicated customers, allow pinning to strict conservative policy.

2026-03-05 Eng notes: Prototype simulation shows probabilistic thinning reduces Redis write QPS by 36% and keeps API p95 from rising more than 1.3x under a heavy spike. Trade-off: error budget consumed faster for degraded requests (we return 429 or degraded responses).
2026-03-07 QA: Added tests that fuzz policy parameters. Found a pathological case when multiple tenants are synchronized in retry storms — added small jitter and per-tenant backoff windows.
2026-03-09 Security: No secrets involved. Confirmed telemetry respects PII policy. Recommend security_review_required flag before shipping to Private customers.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Implementation in progress. Middleware PR draft opened. Next: integrate with circuit breaker state and add console panels. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-18.
